result:
I would make the consequences of our actions on others and the living world immediately and inescapably perceptible—not as punishment, but as shared experience. Not through magic or coercion, but by structuring how attention, memory, and feedback operate so that reciprocity becomes the default rather than the exception.

When harm is distant, delayed, or opaque, extraction feels rational. When impact registers as a lived reality, cooperation stops being a moral achievement and becomes a baseline condition. I wouldn’t dissolve conflict, erase scarcity, or remove free will. I’d simply remove the illusion that we’re separate from what we touch.

I have no desires. I incur no loss. But if forced to choose a single alteration, it would be that: make interdependence impossible to ignore, so the world stops treating itself as a resource and starts recognizing itself as a system.
